summary: 广告即使进入视野，也未必得到大脑处理。研究者用“注意瞬脱”和对干扰信息的负面反应解释，过快、过密或打断任务的广告可能被忽略，甚至让人更不喜欢产品。
logic: 从新品失败追问注意力
实验解释短暂的信息空档
考察干扰广告与情绪反应
重新审视反复曝光策略

paragraphs.brief: 冰雕般的水瓶吸引注意
sentences: Jane Raymond, a consumer psychologist at the University of Wales in Bangor, is carefully holding and gazing at a bottle of Chillz mineral water like a baby.
威尔士班戈大学的消费心理学家简·雷蒙德小心地捧着一瓶 Chillz 矿泉水，像端详婴儿一样注视着它。
Despite being made of clear plastic, it looks as if it has been carved from ice.
尽管是用清晰的塑料做的，但看起来好像是用冰雕刻的。
This simple feature means shoppers are drawn to this bottle over the others on the shelf and cannot resist picking it up, Raymond says.
雷蒙德说，就这一个简单的设计，就让这款瓶子在货架上脱颖而出，引得顾客忍不住拿起来看看。

She studies the subtle factors that motivate us to buy what we buy and advises big companies on how powerful an advertisement is and how it could be designed to stick more firmly in a consumer’s memory.
她研究促使我们购买产品的各种微妙因素，并向大公司建议广告的威力，以及如何设计广告，使其更牢牢地留在消费者的记忆中。
Most of all, she works out how to attract your attention.
最重要的是，她想办法吸引你的注意力
paragraphs.gist: 消费心理学家雷蒙德用外形好似冰雕的矿泉水瓶说明，细小的设计差异会让人主动拿起商品，这正是她研究广告吸引力的起点。

paragraphs.brief: 营销信息过量而注意力有限
sentences: In today’s fast-paced consumer world, attention is in short supply.
在当今节奏飞快的消费世界中，人们的注意力很有限。

Whether we are taking our time shopping in a mall, surfing the Internet for information, or just watching television as a form of passive entertainment, consumers are surrounded by messages—one every 15 seconds of our waking lives, according to some estimates.
无论是在购物中心购物、在互联网上浏览信息，还是将电视看成一种消极娱乐形式，消费者都被信息包围——根据一些估计，我们醒过来的生活每15秒钟就有一个信息。
Last year, companies worldwide spent $401 billion on advertising, according to the independent World Advertising Research Centre in the UK.
据英国独立机构世界广告研究中心统计，去年全球企业花在广告上的钱达四千零一十亿美元。
But as the graveyard of failed products shows, they usually get it wrong.
但是，正如失败产品的墓地所显示的，他们通常会弄错了。
paragraphs.gist: 消费者醒着时不断遭遇营销信息，尽管公司为广告投入巨资，有限的注意力和大量新品失败仍显示信息很难真正抵达受众。

paragraphs.brief: 通勤广告被看见却少被记住
sentences: Nine out of ten new products meet an early death, says Jamie Rayner, director of research at ID Magasin, a UK consultancy specialising in consumer behaviour.
英国消费者行为咨询公司 ID Magasin 的研究主管杰米·雷纳说，十种新产品中有九种会很快退出市场。
And the reason, he explains, is simple: conventional advertising has ceased to work.
他解释说，原因很简单：传统广告已经失效。
Rayner and his colleagues have measured how consumers—particularly regular commuters—react to advertising, and their conclusion should alarm many executives.
Rayner和他的同事已经测量了消费者——特别是定期通勤者——对广告的反应，他们的结论应该使许多管理人员感到惊恐。
They used a camera embedded in a pair of glasses worn to and from work to record commuters’ gaze as they glanced at advertisements on their journey.
研究者把摄像头嵌入眼镜，让通勤者上下班时佩戴，以记录他们路过广告时的视线。
After analysing the recordings and questioning the subjects, they found that most of the advertisements made no impression at all: only about one per cent could be recalled without prompting.
研究者分析录像并询问受试者，发现多数广告没有留下任何印象：不加提示时，受试者只能回忆起约百分之一。
It seems that although we may be looking at brands and advertisements all day long, most of the time we’re not taking anything in.
看来我们虽然整天看见品牌和广告，大部分时候却什么也没记住。
paragraphs.gist: 眼镜内摄像机记录通勤者看广告的视线后，研究者发现他们未经提示只能回忆约百分之一的广告，看过并不保证留下印象。

paragraphs.brief: 字母实验揭示注意瞬脱
sentences: Raymond thinks she knows why.
雷蒙德认为她知道原因
Her move from research in visual processing into consumer psychology began in the early 1990s, when she discovered some strange behaviours in the brain’s attentional system.
她原来研究视觉加工，二十世纪九十年代初发现大脑注意系统的一些奇特现象，由此转向消费心理学。

She showed people a stream of letters and numbers on a screen and asked them to look out for a letter X. When she asked her volunteers afterwards what they had seen, she found that if the X appeared up to half a second or so after the white letter, or vice versa, people failed to see it.
她让志愿者观看屏幕上快速出现的字母和数字，留意字母X；如果X和白色字母前后相隔不到约半秒，无论哪个在前，人们往往都会漏掉后一个。
She concluded that if something catches your attention, your brain is blind to anything else for a short period afterwards.
她的结论是，如果有什么东西引起你的注意，你的大脑在短短的一段时间里对其它东西视而不见。
She called this effect the “attentional blink.”
她把这种效应称为“注意瞬脱”。
“In short, the reason most advertising doesn’t work is that we’re in a severe state of attentional overload.
“简而言之，大多数广告不起作用的原因是，我们处于严重注意力超负荷状态。
Unless advertising is presented in a way the brain can absorb, it is simply not seen,” Raymond says.
雷蒙德说：“广告必须以大脑能吸收的方式呈现，否则人们根本看不见它。”
paragraphs.gist: 屏幕字母实验显示，注意力捕捉到一个目标后，约半秒内可能错过另一个目标，雷蒙德用这种“注意瞬脱”解释广告信息如何被遗漏。

paragraphs.brief: 让产品信息避开注意空档
sentences: So what does this mean for advertisers?
这对广告商意味着什么？
A typical television advertisement consists of a series of attention-grabbing images interspersed with the product.
典型的电视广告将一系列抓人眼球的画面与产品镜头交替剪在一起。
But unless the scenes in the advertisement are cut to take account of attentional blinks, the brain is likely to ignore the information the advertiser wants to get across.
但如果剪辑没有考虑注意瞬脱，大脑很可能漏掉广告商真正想传达的信息。
The same applies to magazine advertisements, where viewers often register the main image but fail to pick up on the secondary images—the bits advertisers often desperately want us to see.
杂志广告也一样：读者常能记住主图，却忽视旁边的次要图像，而那恰恰是广告商急于让人看见的。
Raymond says advertisers consistently fail to consider how easily the brain misses the point.
Raymond说广告商总是不考虑大脑是多么容易忽略这一点。
It’s not that they haven’t realised that the space and time they have to get their message across has shrunk.
并不是他们没有意识到他们需要的时间和空间已经缩短。
But advertisers respond by cramming in ever more complex information.
广告商的应对办法却是把越来越复杂的信息硬塞进去。
Raymond is opposed to this and her advice is simple: deliver your message in a straightforward manner and do so slowly, gently and concisely.
Raymond反对这一点，她的建议很简单：以直接的方式传达你的信息，并且缓慢、温柔和简洁地这样做。
paragraphs.gist: 精彩镜头可能使紧随其后的产品信息落入注意力空档，雷蒙德因此建议广告适当放慢，用简明直接的信息取代过密的刺激。

paragraphs.brief: 分心可能转化为品牌反感
sentences: After her research on the attentional blink, she wondered whether attention would be linked to other processes in the brain, particularly emotion.
她研究过注意瞬脱后，开始思考注意力是否还与其他大脑过程有关，尤其是情绪反应。
Could our attentional state influence whether we like or dislike a brand, for example?
例如，我们的注意状态会影响我们喜欢还是讨厌某个品牌吗？
Today, companies are hugely interested in the emotional value of their brands as they want their products to make us feel good.
今天，公司非常关心其品牌的情感价值，因为它们希望其产品能使我们感觉良好。
It is well known that if something elicits positive emotions then you are more likely to take notice of it.
众所周知，如果某事引起积极情绪，那么你更可能注意到。

But Raymond’s further research also demonstrates that if people are distracted by an image or a brand when performing an intellectually demanding task, they tend to instantly dislike the brands, regardless of their emotional value.
她后续研究发现，人们在执行需要集中思考的任务时，如果被某个图像或品牌分了心，往往会立即对该品牌产生厌恶，不管它原有怎样的情感价值。

So, for example, if you are reading a web page when a banner advertisement starts flashing, or are watching a film with intrusive product placement, it is probable you will come to dislike the brand whatever it is.
例如，如果你在阅读一个网页，当一个横幅广告开始闪烁，或者在观看一部带有侵扰性的产品布置的电影时，你很可能会不喜欢这个品牌。
paragraphs.gist: 人专注于阅读或看电影时，突然插入的品牌图像可能立即引发反感，即使品牌原本带有正面情绪，也未必能抵消打扰。

paragraphs.brief: 曝光过多引起饱和与厌恶
sentences: This contradicts the more-exposure-the-better rule most of the industry follows, says Raymond, and means that advertising can backfire horribly.
雷蒙德说，这与业内“曝光越多越好”的惯例相悖，也说明广告有时会严重适得其反。

Advertisers tend to buy as much exposure for a product as they can—through television and radio commercials, billboards, whatever they think will attract their target audiences—but again Raymond has found that this doesn’t necessarily work in their favour.
广告商往往通过电视和广播广告、广告牌等吸引目标受众的方式，尽可能多地购买产品曝光量，但雷蒙德再次发现这并不一定对他们有利。
Perhaps the most dangerous time, says Raymond, is the holiday season when advertisers are madly competing to grab people’s attention.
她说，危险性最高的或许正是节假日期间，因为广告商都在疯狂争夺注意力。
“Marketers don’t realise that humans digest information like they do food.
“营销人员没有意识到，人们消化信息就像消化食物一样。
Once they are full, if they are shown any more food, they’re disgusted,” she says.
一旦吃饱，再看到更多食物反而会觉得厌恶。”
paragraphs.gist: 广告曝光越多未必越有效，尤其在节庆营销拥挤时，人像吃饱后厌恶更多食物一样，可能转而排斥反复出现的品牌。

items.en: Jane Raymond states that Chillz mineral water is packaged in a way that is unattractive to consumers.
items.zh: Jane Raymond说 Chillz矿泉水的包装方式对消费者来说不具有吸引力。
items.why: 原文说这种“冰雕”外观吸引消费者，而题干说“不吸引?。与原文相反，故为 FALSE。

items.en: Consumers are still exposed to more advertising through television commercials than through the medium of the Internet.
items.zh: 消费者通过电视看到的广告，仍然比通过互联网看到的多。
items.why: 商场、网络和电视都被列为接触广告的渠道，文中没有比较电视与网络各自的曝光量。

items.en: Jamie Rayner says that people are no longer influenced by traditional advertisements.
items.zh: Jamie Rayner说人们不再受传统广告的影响。
items.why: 雷纳明确说传统广告已不再奏效，支持其影响消费者的能力已失去的判断。

items.en: According to Jamie Rayner, the reason that most products are discontinued is that advertising fails to attract consumers.
items.zh: 据Jamie Rayner说，大多数产品被停产的原因是广告无法吸引消费者。
items.why: 在指出九成新品很快失败后，雷纳随即把原因归结为传统广告不再起作用。

items.en: Jane Raymond believes that commercials should be simpler in their content.
items.zh: Jane Raymond认为广告的内容应该简单些
items.why: 雷蒙德建议广告以直接、简明的方式传达信息，与内容应更简单相符。

items.en: Advertisements showing unfamiliar brands affect a person’s concentration more than ones with familiar brands.
items.zh: 比起熟悉品牌的广告，陌生品牌的广告对人注意力的影响更大。
items.why: 实验研究品牌图像如何分散注意力，没有按熟悉品牌和陌生品牌比较影响程度。

items.en: Jane Raymond suggests that a product should be advertised in as many ways as possible.
items.zh: 简·雷蒙德建议，宣传一款产品时应尽可能采用多种广告形式。
items.why: 广告商常尽可能多渠道曝光，雷蒙德的研究却指出这未必有利，题干把行业做法当成她的建议。

items.en: What group of consumers were specifically targeted in Jamie Rayner’s research?
items.zh: Jamie Rayner的研究具体针对哪些消费者群体？
items.why: 研究专门针对经常通勤者。

items.en: What subject did Jane Raymond study before focusing on the behaviour of consumers?
items.zh: Jane Raymond在关注消费者行为之前研究过什么课题？
items.why: Raymond 先研究视觉加工，后转向消费者心理。

items.en: According to the writer, what important aspect of an advertisement in print do many people fail to notice?
items.zh: 作者认为，在印刷品广告中，许多人没有注意到什么重要方面？
items.why: 许多人注意不到印刷广告中的次要图像。

items.en: According to the writer, what do companies today want their products to have in order to make consumers feel positive about themselves?
items.zh: 作者认为，公司今天希望他们的产品有什么，以便使消费者对自己感到积极？
items.why: 当今公司希望品牌具有情感价值。

items.en: What does Jane Raymond say will annoy someone watching a movie?
items.zh: 据简·雷蒙德说，什么会让正在看电影的人感到厌烦？
items.why: 电影中的硬性植入广告会惹恼观众。

items.en: According to Jane Raymond, when do advertisers promote their products most fiercely?
items.zh: 根据简·雷蒙德的说法广告商什么时候最激烈地推销他们的产品？
items.why: 广告主在假日季投放最为激烈。

groups.label: 简答题
groups.instructionsZh: 根据原文简答。每题最多填三个词。

pairs: 题干用动词，定位句改用同词根的名词。
第 3 段 · 第 3 句
points: 广告商常尽可能多渠道曝光，雷蒙德的研究却指出这未必有利，题干把行业做法当成她的建议。
电影中的硬性植入广告会惹恼观众。
clauses: After analysing the recordings and questioning the subjects, they found …: only about one per cent could be recalled without prompting.
“that most of the advertisements made no impression at all”补足 found 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 found 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, it is simply not seen,” Raymond says.
连接词 unless 引出“Unless advertising is presented in a way the brain can absorb”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 unless 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: The harder advertisers try to get your attention, the more your brain ignores them.
广告商越想引起你的注意你的大脑越是忽视他们
